Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Inscribe-and-erase: chromatin accessibility time course after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Give cells a brief pulse of a stimulus that induces AP-1 (FOS/JUN), such as serum, TPA or injury. Then track ATAC-seq, CUT&Tag for AP-1 and H3K27ac, and RNA-seq for days to weeks after AP-1 itself has returned to baseline. Like a word inscribed in stone, a memory mechanism would leave persistent open 'AP-1 motif' sites that outlast the signal. Compare these with naive cells to test whether the marks last and whether they change a second response.

ideas.title: Eustatic 'sea-level' test: primed versus naive re-stimulation with acute AP-1 degradation
ideas.description: Eustatic change is a lasting shift in baseline after the cause has gone. By analogy, stimulate cells twice, with a rest interval between. Measure whether the second transcriptional response is faster or larger than the first. Then use degron-tagged (dTAG/auxin) FOS or JUN to remove AP-1 either during priming or only during the rest period. This separates AP-1 as the writer of the memory from AP-1 as the reader or maintainer of it.

ideas.title: Flooding versus trickle: dose-and-duration single-cell live imaging
ideas.description: Use live reporters (FOS-GFP, AP-1 transcriptional reporters, JUN-N-terminal-kinase sensors) in single cells. Give pulsed, 'flooding' or escalating inputs. Test whether the history of AP-1 activity, such as its dynamics, cumulative integral and frequency, predicts later gene expression and cell fate better than current AP-1 levels do. Analyze with information-theoretic and hysteresis measures, and look for cell-lineage inheritance of states in daughter cells after division.

ideas.title: Entangled loci: allele-resolved single-cell multiome and Hi-C/Micro-C of AP-1 targets
ideas.description: In stimulated and rested cells, use single-cell ATAC plus RNA with Micro-C or HiChIP to ask whether AP-1 binding leaves lasting enhancer-promoter contacts and nucleosome remodeling (BAF recruitment). Then use dCas9 or motif mutation to 'underlap' the AP-1 site at individual enhancers. If the site is required for persistent accessibility and for the faster second response, that is evidence for a locus-specific memory. Allele-specific edits give within-cell controls.

ideas.title: Predict-then-test: computational model of memory with perturbation validation
ideas.description: Fit a mechanistic model (for example a bistable feedback or a chromatin-state model) to time-resolved AP-1 occupancy, accessibility and expression data. Use it to predict which loci hold memory and how long it lasts, and what happens when AP-1 or its co-factors are removed or overexpressed. Test the predictions with held-out tissue data, such as wounded epidermis, neurons after activity, or T cells. Compare AP-1-dependent memory against alternatives such as histone marks, DNA methylation and other pioneer factors, using ablation of each.
